hero.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound seconds before train arrives
hero.teaser: Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing arm and pulled a trapped driver to safety seconds before a train passed through the intersection at Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway i
hero.body:
Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing arm and pulled a trapped driver to safety seconds before a train passed through the intersection at Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound on Friday evening around 5 p.m. Debbie Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm came down on top of her car, trapping her on the tracks. Her car's antenna was caught on the crossing arm.

Baur, 23, was driving home to Port Saint Lucie from work when he stopped at the crossing and saw Spoelstra's red car stuck between the gates. Dash cam video from a nearby driver captured the moment Baur ran across the tracks toward Spoelstra's car as a train approached. Baur lifted the crossing arm with both arms, allowing Spoelstra to reverse her car away from the tracks just before the train came through on her side of the tracks.

Lizzy Dominguez witnessed the rescue from her car behind Baur's vehicle at the crossing. After the rescue, Dominguez took a photo of Baur and posted it on social media to find and thank him. Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing on Sunday and hugged when they saw each other.

Spoelstra reported the crossing arm malfunction to Florida East Coast Railway and was told someone would inspect the gate. Spoelstra plans to take Baur and his family out for dinner as a thank you. She noted that her 9-month-old grandson shares the same name as her rescuer, Josiah.

cards.headline: Daytona Tortugas rally to beat St. Lucie Mets 5-4, take series at Clover Park
cards.teaser: The Daytona Tortugas defeated the St. Lucie Mets 5-4 on Sunday at Clover Park, winning the seven-game series 4-3. The Tortugas scored five runs across the fourth and fifth innings
cards.body:
The Daytona Tortugas defeated the St. Lucie Mets 5-4 on Sunday at Clover Park, winning the seven-game series 4-3. The Tortugas scored five runs across the fourth and fifth innings to build a 5-0 lead before holding off a late Mets rally.

Mets starter Joel Lara cruised through the first three innings, allowing just one baserunner on a walk. Lara struggled in the fourth, walking the first three batters. A wild pitch brought home Ichiro Cano for the first run. Anielson Buten hit a two-run single with two outs to make it 3-0. Cano hit the first pitch from reliever Jean Brito for a two-run homer in the fifth inning that made it 5-0.

The Mets mounted a comeback in the sixth inning when Elian Pea led off with a double against Lisnerkin Lantigua, extending his hitting streak to 11 games. Kuhio Aloy ripped a two-run double with two outs to get the Mets on the board, and Simon Juan followed with an RBI single to make it 5-3. Juan added a sacrifice fly in the eighth to pull the Mets within one at 5-4.

Daytona pitchers Lantigua and Jesus Colina retired the last six Mets batters in a row to secure the win. Colina earned his first save by retiring the side in order in the ninth with a fly out and back-to-back strikeouts. The Mets fell to 16-25 in the second half and 49-58 overall. They begin a six-game commuter series at the Jupiter Hammerheads on Tuesday with first pitch at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium set for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Indian River County schools open Monday with some bus pickups before sunrise
cards.teaser: Public schools in Indian River County open Monday, Aug. 10, for the 2026-2027 school year, with high schools starting at 7:20 a.m., middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m., and elem
cards.body:
Indian River County public schools begin the 2026-2027 school year on Monday, with buses picking up students sometimes in the dark. High schools open their doors to students at 7:20 a.m., middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m., and elementary schools at 9 a.m. Many students will be walking to bus stops in the dark on a daily basis as the days grow shorter. Students who meet the bus at the stop near State Road 60 and Rollins Ranch Road are scheduled for pickup at 5:51 a.m., according to Dr. Kyra Schafte, executive director of the school district's strategic communications and marketing.

The School District and Indian River County Sheriff's Office are urging caution regarding school bus safety throughout the year. Sheriff Eric Flowers said in a video posted on the sheriff's office Facebook page that all schools are changing and new students entering schools will go through metal detectors. He asked parents to be patient during drop off periods. Flowers said all of the safety measures will take some time for everyone to get used to.

Vehicles traveling in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped to pick up or discharge children at two-lane paved roads and at multi-lane paved roads without a raised median or physical barrier. As of May 1, Florida began issuing citations for illegal passing of a stopped school bus with stop arm extended and red lights flashing, with a $225 fine for the offense. For a second or subsequent offense within five years, the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles may suspend a driver's license for 90 days up to 6 months.

School district officials recommend children arrive at the bus stop at least 10 minutes early and stay at least 10 feet away from the roadway while waiting. Parents who drive their children to bus stops should park a safe distance away from buses during both morning pickup and afternoon drop off to help maintain clear visibility and safe loading areas. Transportation details are available on the Indian River County schools webpage at www.indianriverschools.org/o/sdirc/page/transportation, as well as the district's Facebook and Instagram accounts.

cards.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
cards.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.headline: Missing 14-year-old autistic boy Ethan Boyd safely located, Martin County sheriff says
cards.teaser: Ethan Boyd, a missing 14-year-old autistic boy, was safely located at 11:44 p.m., according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office.
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff’s Office had asked the public for help locating Ethan Boyd, a 14-year-old autistic boy who went missing Wednesday in Palm City. Ethan was last seen at 5:20 p.m. running toward the south side of the Grand Oaks senior living community near Coquina Cove.

Ethan was described as 5 feet 7 inches tall, weighing approximately 130 pounds, with brown hair. He was last seen wearing a dark blue shirt and seafoam green shorts without shoes.

The sheriff’s office asked anyone who saw Ethan to contact deputies immediately. The agency later updated its original Facebook post to announce that he had been safely located.

hero.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound seconds before train arrives
hero.teaser: Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing arm and pulled a trapped driver to safety seconds before a train passed through the intersection at Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway i
hero.body:
Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing arm and pulled a trapped driver to safety seconds before a train passed through the intersection at Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound on Friday evening around 5 p.m. Debbie Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm came down on top of her car, trapping her on the tracks. Her car's antenna was caught on the crossing arm.

Baur, 23, was driving home to Port Saint Lucie from work when he stopped at the crossing and saw Spoelstra's red car stuck between the gates. Dash cam video from a nearby driver captured the moment Baur ran across the tracks toward Spoelstra's car as a train approached. Baur lifted the crossing arm with both arms, allowing Spoelstra to reverse her car away from the tracks just before the train came through on her side of the tracks.

Lizzy Dominguez witnessed the rescue from her car behind Baur's vehicle at the crossing. After the rescue, Dominguez took a photo of Baur and posted it on social media to find and thank him. Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing on Sunday and hugged when they saw each other.

Spoelstra reported the crossing arm malfunction to Florida East Coast Railway and was told someone would inspect the gate. Spoelstra plans to take Baur and his family out for dinner as a thank you. She noted that her 9-month-old grandson shares the same name as her rescuer, Josiah.

hero.headline: Indian River County schools open Monday with some bus pickups before sunrise
hero.teaser: Public schools in Indian River County open Monday, Aug. 10, for the 2026-2027 school year, with high schools starting at 7:20 a.m., middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m., and elem
hero.body:
Indian River County public schools begin the 2026-2027 school year on Monday, with buses picking up students sometimes in the dark. High schools open their doors to students at 7:20 a.m., middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m., and elementary schools at 9 a.m. Many students will be walking to bus stops in the dark on a daily basis as the days grow shorter. Students who meet the bus at the stop near State Road 60 and Rollins Ranch Road are scheduled for pickup at 5:51 a.m., according to Dr. Kyra Schafte, executive director of the school district's strategic communications and marketing.

The School District and Indian River County Sheriff's Office are urging caution regarding school bus safety throughout the year. Sheriff Eric Flowers said in a video posted on the sheriff's office Facebook page that all schools are changing and new students entering schools will go through metal detectors. He asked parents to be patient during drop off periods. Flowers said all of the safety measures will take some time for everyone to get used to.

Vehicles traveling in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped to pick up or discharge children at two-lane paved roads and at multi-lane paved roads without a raised median or physical barrier. As of May 1, Florida began issuing citations for illegal passing of a stopped school bus with stop arm extended and red lights flashing, with a $225 fine for the offense. For a second or subsequent offense within five years, the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles may suspend a driver's license for 90 days up to 6 months.

School district officials recommend children arrive at the bus stop at least 10 minutes early and stay at least 10 feet away from the roadway while waiting. Parents who drive their children to bus stops should park a safe distance away from buses during both morning pickup and afternoon drop off to help maintain clear visibility and safe loading areas. Transportation details are available on the Indian River County schools webpage at www.indianriverschools.org/o/sdirc/page/transportation, as well as the district's Facebook and Instagram accounts.
